- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Sopranos' plot points and storylines were inspired by real-life cases and events involving law enforcement and organized crime.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The character of Tony Soprano is loosely based on real-life New Jersey mob boss Vincent "Vinny Ocean" Palermo.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The show's portrayal of the FBI's attempts to infiltrate organized crime was inspired by real-life investigations of the Genovese and Lucchese crime families in New York City.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The show depicted everyday workings of organized crime, such as the use of "front" businesses to launder money and the Mafia's strict code of silence, based on real-life practices.
- [USER] User inquired if the writers of The Sopranos met with real-life law enforcement officials or people involved in organized crime for inspiration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The writers of The Sopranos met with real-life law enforcement officials and people involved in organized crime for inspiration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] David Chase, the show's creator, conducted extensive research and interviews with former FBI agents and members of organized crime.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some interviews were conducted in person, while others were done over the phone.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The writers consulted with experts in psychology and addiction to accurately depict mental health struggles and substance abuse issues faced by characters.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some real-life people who inspired characters in The Sopranos have commented on the show.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Vincent "Vinny Ocean" Palermo gave an interview to the New York Post in 1999, stating the show was "pretty accurate" but pointed out some inaccuracies regarding mobster altercations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Former FBI agent Joe Pistone, who went undercover as a mob associate, praised the show's portrayal of both the Mafia and law enforcement in an interview with The Daily Beast in 2014.
